entries.title: Deadly shooting near Paris is a 'racist terrorist attack', Macron says
entries.snippet: One person is killed and five wounded in a series of attacks. The suspected gunman has been apprehended.

entries.title: Seven shot dead by gunmen at church funeral in Jordan, officials say
entries.snippet: Thirty-four people are also injured in the attack in southern Karak governorate, and a manhunt is now under way.

entries.title: Freed US citizen was tortured in Russian jail, former Ukrainian prisoners say
entries.snippet: Ukrainians held alongside the American say they witnessed beatings and sexual humiliation by Russian guards during his detention.

entries.title: Israeli forces begin demolishing Palestinian buildings in Hebron after two Israeli soldiers shot dead
entries.snippet: The soldiers were killed in an attack by two Palestinian gunmen at a checkpoint outside the West Bank city on Friday morning.

entries.title: White House says Melania Trump brokered truce for Ukraine city 'on brink of disaster'
entries.snippet: Ukraine and Russia confirm the truce in Russian-occupied Oleshky, where residents have had to eat garden weeds to survive.

entries.title: Argentina drops investigation into President Milei over crypto fraud
entries.snippet: Javier Milei had denied acting fraudulently when a cryptocurrency nosedived after he deleted a social media post about it.

entries.title: Oil spill washes up on UAE beaches after tanker strike
entries.snippet: Satellite images show oil spreading for miles along the coastline, threatening local marine wildlife

entries.title: Ukraine says Starlink still restricted after Trump says limits lifted
entries.snippet: The network is used by the Ukrainian military, sources say, and Trump says "if there is a problem, I'll get it straightened out".

entries.title: Denmark to ban mink farming in government U-turn
entries.snippet: Once the world's largest producer of mink pelts, the nation's industry has declined in recent years.

entries.title: PSG v Lyon moved as Paris prepares for more protests
entries.snippet: Paris St-Germain's Ligue 1 match against Lyon at the Parc des Princes is pushed back 24 hours as the French capital prepares for another weekend of protests.

entries.title: Cyprus police open investigation into financial affairs of Roman Abramovich
entries.snippet: Questions about the integrity of some of Abramovich's professional advisers, were raised earlier this month.

entries.title: Woman with Ebola in Nigeria confirmed as wife of Swiss diplomat
entries.snippet: Her husband is currently in isolation but has not developed any symptoms, Swiss officials say.

entries.title: Watch: CCTV footage shows gunmen near church in Jordan
entries.snippet: Dozens of people had been inside the church for a funeral when the shooting began, local media report.

entries.title: Doctors tell the BBC about the targeting of Sudanese hospitals by paramilitary fighters
entries.snippet: A BBC investigation has found evidence that Sudanese paramilitary fighters systematically destroyed el-Fasher's healthcare system.

entries.title: Blue Planet III: Moment octopus escapes death after hunt gone wrong
entries.snippet: The sequence is part of the latest Blue Planet series from Sir David Attenborough.

entries.title: 'It's part of the culture' - New York bans horse-drawn carriages after more than 160 years
entries.snippet: The BBC's Madeline Halpert spoke to city tourists, residents and horse carriage workers about the industry and their opinion on the ban.

entries.title: Damaging hail pelts Phoenix in rare storm
entries.snippet: Videos from the Arizona capital show people sheltering inside a car as hail smashes the windscreen, while intense downpours covered neighbourhoods in ice.

entries.title: Hispanic voters helped bring Trump to power - in Texas, the tide may be turning
entries.snippet: Recent polls suggest the president is facing challenging headwinds in the state ahead of the midterms.

entries.title: Rubio turns to small Indian town as US faces high oil prices
entries.snippet: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio pushed a business and energy agenda over diplomacy on his second trip to India this year.

entries.title: Attack on actor Tiger Shroff is dark reminder of Bollywood's gangster past
entries.snippet: The attack on Shroff has revived memories of the 1990s, when gangsters wielded influence over the industry.

entries.title: Severe flooding hits Four Corners region, more expected through the weekend
entries.snippet: Intense rainfall slammed the Four Corners region late this week. As rivers flooded, towns declared evacuations and emergencies and made rescues.

entries.title: The Pentagon's guidelines for "responsible AI" aren't always followed, report shows
entries.snippet: The Pentagon is building weapons and projects with AI capabilities that officials say don't always closely adhere to the agency's own guidelines for AI, according to a congressional watchdog report published in October.

entries.title: Ohio could decide control of the Senate. Its rural voters might decide the winner
entries.snippet: Ohio has been a reliably red state for several elections but it's competitive this year. If Democrats want to prevail, they'll have to win people who have backed Republicans, like rural voters.

entries.title: A D.C. park was made 'for the pleasure of the people.' Trump's plan would change that
entries.snippet: Trump's most recent rendering of East Potomac Park overtakes the D.C. peninsula with a sprawling golf course, without the grassy areas and road beloved by locals. That's prompted grassroots pushback.

entries.title: Ex-FBI employees charged with lying to Congress over Hunter Biden inquiries
entries.snippet: Republicans have long accused the FBI of mishandling the laptop and the investigations into the younger Biden.

entries.title: Will a macaque eat a grape sitting on a pile of poo? A study on germophobia
entries.snippet: When an outbreak strikes, humans try to avoid germs. (Remember wiping off groceries at the start of the pandemic?) What about ... monkeys?

entries.title: Authorities investigating whether first Kenya and Nigeria Ebola cases crossed paths
entries.snippet: Nigeria this week recorded its first case of Ebola in the current outbreak, which has spread from the epicenter in Congo to several other African countries.

entries.title: Military reinforcements move to Mideast. And, millions of Americans vote early
entries.snippet: Military reinforcements are heading to the Middle East and some personnel have left the region, pointing to a potential attack on Iran. And, millions of Americans have already voted in the midterms.

entries.title: Why Meta is charging to post more hyperlinks
entries.snippet: Social media sites aren't the biggest fans of people leaving via hyperlinks. In fact, Meta has made it subscription-worthy for a Facebook Page to post more than two hyperlinks per month. What's the rationale for companies want to keep you on their site?

entries.title: Israel orders closure of West Bank after soldiers kill 2 men behind an alleged attack
entries.snippet: Israeli soldiers shot and killed two men who the military said had launched an attack near the city of Hebron in the occupied West Bank on Friday morning. At least five people were injured, including some critically.

entries.title: Rollins says USDA is 'full-bore ahead' on Forest Service reorganization
entries.snippet: The Trump administration wants to move Forest Service headquarters from Washington to Salt Lake City, shutter 23 research stations, and close many regional offices and replace them with state offices.

entries.title: Signs of fraying loyalty emerge in Netanyahu stronghold before Israeli election
entries.snippet: Kiryat Shmona, Israel's northernmost city, has long been a bastion of support for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party. But that loyalty is no longer ironclad.

entries.title: Treasury proposes rule to curb high-tech investments in China and other adversaries
entries.snippet: The U.S. Treasury Department proposed a rule Thursday to crack down on American high-tech investments such as supercomputing and artificial intelligence in China, Russia, North Korea and other "countries of concern."

entries.title: Trump says he ordered suit to block Alaska Senate results if GOP loses

entries.title: Brazil's high-stakes presidential runoff could reshape country's future
entries.snippet: This weekend, voters in Brazil head to the polls in a high-stakes presidential runoff that could reshape that country's political future. Will Brazil join a rightward shift across parts of the Americas, or stick with its left-wing leadership? Voting is compulsory for most adults,

entries.title: Medicare Advantage cuts leave millions scrambling to find coverage
entries.snippet: Health care costs are climbing, putting new pressure on millions of Americans and raising questions about the coverage they can afford. The challenges extend to Medicare Advantage. In some parts of the country, insurers are pulling out of markets or eliminating plans that many re

entries.title: Why 'You Can See Everything' is captivating audiences
entries.snippet: "You Can See Everything," the documentary co-directed by Lance Oppenheim and Nathan Fielder, is a breakthrough success. It follows Elizabeth Holmes, the convicted founder of Theranos, just weeks before she goes to prison. The intimate access and the questions it raises are the ta

entries.title: Defense attorneys in case over Charlie Kirk's killing say they need years to prepare for trial
entries.snippet: Defense attorneys for the man accused of assassinating conservative activist Charlie Kirk are suggesting a 2029 trial date because they say it could take them that long to prepare their case.

entries.title: WATCH: Trump defends Musk on Starlink disturbances, says he'll 'never do anything wrong'
entries.snippet: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Friday that service remained slow from Starshield, SpaceX's military-grade version of the Starlink satellite internet service.

entries.title: WATCH: Trump at GOP rally in Florida revives idea of military intervention in Cuba after Iran
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump on Friday told a rally for candidates in South Florida that U.S. warships returning from the Middle East could stop over in Cuba on their way back from the Iran war, his latest suggestion of taking an interventionist approach to the nearby country.

entries.title: Oregon father who killed school shooter says he regrets there were children he didn't save
entries.snippet: Kaylub Giamanco, whose two daughters attend Silver Rail Elementary, where the Oct. 15 attack occurred, said he was the children's "last line of defense" and that he regrets not arriving soon enough to save them all.

entries.title: Why experts are pushing RFK Jr. to release a federal definition of ultraprocessed foods
entries.snippet: More than 100 science, medical and nutrition experts signed and sent an open letter Friday to the Office of Management and Budget, urging the administration to release the first-ever government definition of ultraprocessed foods.

entries.title: DOJ has monitored elections for decades. Here's why some state officials are concerned this year
entries.snippet: The agency regularly monitors polling places. But this year's effort on Nov. 3 will more than double the number of federal monitors deployed during the 2022 midterms.

entries.title: Police officer who shot and killed 1-year-old boy in Mississippi has resigned, mayor says
entries.snippet: Sgt. Hunter Foster, 33, had been cleared of criminal wrongdoing by the Mississippi Attorney General's office earlier this week after its monthslong probe concluded his use of force had been justified.

entries.title: Trump administration stopped sharing evidence in Good and Pretti killings, Minnesota officials say
entries.snippet: The Trump administration has suggested that state prosecutors don't have jurisdiction to investigate federal officers, while Minnesota officials have said they don't trust the federal government to investigate itself.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Ebola: Kenya announces second death
entries.snippet: Kenyan health officials said the 65-year-old ​woman was a close ‌relative of a ‌​man who died of Ebola last month. The woman developed symptoms ‌while under quarantine in Nairobi.

entries.title: Trump eases Canada tariffs ahead of US midterms
entries.snippet: The move comes as Trump's Republican Party scrambles to maintain control of the US Congress, with a Republican candidate in a key Senate race saying she had lobbied to lift the tariffs on Canadian products.

entries.title: Russia's attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, are intensifying. DW asked people on the ground what life is like
entries.snippet: Russia's attacks on the Ukrainian capital are hitting harder and more frequently, making 2026 one of the long war's bloodiest years for Kyiv. DW asked people on the ground what life is like.

entries.title: Jordan: Karak church shooting leaves 7 dead, dozens injured
entries.snippet: A shooting at a Greek Orthodox church in southern Jordan happened during a funeral, according to authorities. Two unidentified men opened fire on the procession, with Jordan's king vowing "the harshest retaliation."

entries.title: Russia, Ukraine agree to US-brokered, 1 city ceasefire
entries.snippet: The Ukrainian city of Oleshky, occupied by Russia and on the frontline, faces a humanitarian crisis. The localized truce comes as Ukrainian President Zelenskyy said negotiators would meet for wider talks next month.

entries.title: Afghan women could lose one of their last paths to a higher education
entries.snippet: The US has defunded one of the last universities giving Afghan women the chance to receive an education after the Taliban takeover in 2021. DW spoke with a student who says she's lost hope of ever earning a degree.

entries.title: Romania blames Russia for ship attack in the Black Sea
entries.snippet: Russian strikes against ships attempting to export Ukrainian grain and cargo through the western Black Sea have sharply increased this month.

entries.title: Ukraine tries to shut Moscow's airports with drone strikes on Russia
entries.snippet: Repeated Ukrainian drone attacks are increasingly disrupting operations at Moscow's airports. The pounding is part of Ukraine's plan to shut down Russia's airpace.

entries.title: Many feared trapped under collapsed building in Nairobi
entries.snippet: People are feared to be trapped after a large, unfinished building in Nairobi collapsed during construction. Rescue operations have proven complicated as police fired tear gas to disperse looters.

entries.title: Japan-Russia ties erode as journalist sits in Moscow jail
entries.snippet: Japan is demanding access to a journalist who was arrested by Russian security services. The Kremlin claims that Japan is using journalists as spies.

entries.title: Uganda says it has no active Ebola cases, but infections in Kenya and Nigeria are prompting fresh scrutiny
entries.snippet: Health officials are investigating whether Ebola patients in Kenya and Nigeria crossed paths at Uganda's main airport as conflicting accounts cloud the source of one infection.

entries.title: Serbia: Hope, tension and apprehension as voters prepare to elect new parliament
entries.snippet: After two years of protests, Serbia faces a pivotal election on Sunday, with a student-led challenge to Aleksandar Vucic's lengthy rule. Allegations of electoral irregularities and fears of a post-election crisis abound.

entries.title: France: 1 killed, 4 wounded after shooting near Paris
entries.snippet: French police arrested a suspect after gunshots were fired on the outskirts of Paris in what President Macron described as a racist and terrorist attack.

entries.title: Sri Lanka: Death of iconic elephant raises habitat concerns
entries.snippet: The death of what was thought to be Sri Lanka’s largest elephant has drawn attention to human-elephant conflict in rural communities. The island country sees a high number of deadly encounters.

entries.title: Greece joins countries putting age-limits on social media, banning access for kids under 15
entries.snippet: Greece has passed legislation banning social media access for children under 15. New rules will come into effect on January 1, 2027, and are designed to protect children's mental health.

entries.title: Germany news: Wadephul says 'threat of famine' due to ongoing wars
entries.snippet: German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul is joining counterparts in Turkey for discussions on a range of interlinked geopolitical crises. Back in Germany, the Bavarian CSU party begins its two-day conference in Munich.

entries.title: Israel orders home demolitions after soldiers killed in West Bank
entries.snippet: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israeli forces will demolish homes in the West Bank after gunmen killed two Israeli soldiers in the West Bank city of Hebron.

entries.title: South Korea proposes military talks with North again
entries.snippet: South Korea is attempting to mutually determine the land border with North Korea amid military incidents and escalating tensions.

entries.title: Germany sit out FIFA Under-15 World Cup as Russia return
entries.snippet: Germany is one a handful of FIFA's 211 nations to refuse an invitation to play at the inaugural Under-15 World Cup. The tournament will also mark Russia's return to the FIFA fold.
